solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nonsense talked about approved fairy stories kept here?

indicators.note: the nonsense word goes round, so it is about the approval

parts.note: bosh is nonsense talk
OK means approved
an elf is a fairy

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at fairy stories that someone has approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy stories' looks like one phrase, but 'fairy' is wordplay and only 'stories kept here?' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Books of stories are stored on a shelf, so this is a cryptic description by function.

clue.text: Put identifying mark on torch

definitions.meaning: to mark livestock or goods with an owner's sign
a burning stick used as a light

explanation.surface: Someone is told to label a torch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a mark burnt on cattle, and a burning piece of wood used as a light.

clue.text: Abroad, old group's unable to operate

parts.note: abroad means out, away from home
a faction is a group within a party

explanation.surface: An old group overseas finds itself unable to function.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of action is the idiom for a machine or person temporarily unable to work.

clue.text: 3 Religious instruction accepted by dramatist that supplies dope

indicators.note: the dramatist takes in the instruction, so it goes inside the playwright's name

parts.note: J. M. Synge, the Irish playwright
RI is the school abbreviation for religious instruction

explanation.surface: A playwright who took religious classes is accused of dealing drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '3' at the start is a leftover of the clue's numbering, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is a drug, and a hypodermic needle is the device that injects such drugs.

clue.text: This writer knocked back pub drink in anger

indicators.note: in a down clue the pronoun is turned upside down, read the other way

parts.note: the setter calls himself me
bitter is a kind of British beer served in pubs

explanation.surface: The writer downed a drink in the pub out of fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses ME to EM. Bitter is a hoppy British ale.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to make them resentful, a near synonym for angering them.

clue.text: Housewife's talk, not entirely joyous

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: A housewife's chatter is not wholly cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Festal means festive or celebratory, close in sense to joyful.

clue.text: A question of identity, both hands showing fingerprint feature

parts.note: who? asks who someone is
R and L stand for right and left hands

explanation.surface: An identity check where both hands reveal fingerprints.
explanation.definitionFit: A whorl is a spiral ridge pattern, one of the main patterns in fingerprints.

clue.text: Sound a warning, perhaps, when crossing street

indicators.note: the word for when goes across, enclosing the street

parts.note: while means during the time when

explanation.surface: A lollipop warden blows a warning while crossing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a whistle is only one way to sound a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle is blown, by a referee or guard, as one example of a warning signal.

clue.text: Member of parliament fed up with Liberal decline

indicators.note: the Liberal sinks, going down to the foot of this down entry

parts.note: feeling low means fed up, depressed

explanation.surface: An MP tired of his party's waning fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' moves the L of LOW to the bottom. A group of these birds is called a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls, so each bird is one member.

clue.text: Churchman responsible for poetry recital?

definitions.meaning: a lay person licensed to lead services
a lay is a poem, so its reader recites poetry

explanation.surface: A clergyman is put in charge of reading verse aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensed lay minister in the Church, and whimsically a person who reads lays, old narrative poems.

clue.text: Notable first female priest's powerless

indicators.note: without power, and P is the physics symbol for power, so it is dropped

parts.note: a pastor is a minister or priest

explanation.surface: A pioneering woman priest finds herself without authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the UK House of Commons, in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Astor was famous as the first female MP to sit in Parliament.

clue.text: I set on first mate in savage fashion

indicators.note: the I is placed on the end of the word for first

parts.note: best means first, top
an ally is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to attacking their best friend brutally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set on' looks like attacking, but it only places I after BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestially means like a beast, brutally or savagely.

clue.text: The deficient retail supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble about the shortfall in shop stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun about stock, but it is the adverb 'in a supple way', signalling the anagram of DEFICIENT RETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatically, 'the' is the example of this article in English.

clue.text: Remembers what visiting carer does?

definitions.meaning: a home carer visits, minding someone

explanation.surface: A care worker on a home visit recalls things.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means recalls, and literally a carer calls on someone to look after them.

clue.text: Absurd noun dropped by Eastenders' editor?

indicators.note: the noun is let fall from the rest of the phrase

parts.note: East Enders of London are cockneys
n is the grammar abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A soap's editor cuts a noun from the script.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are traditional working-class Londoners from the East End; EastEnders is also a British TV soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockeyed means crazy or preposterous, a synonym of absurd.

clue.text: Commander improving without first getting organised

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for improving is removed

parts.note: edifying means morally improving

explanation.surface: An officer improves things without consulting first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without first' drops the E of EDIFYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Codifying means arranging rules into a system, so putting them in order.

clue.text: Devious devil touring East in disguise

indicators.note: the scrambled word travels round, going around the compass point
devious, winding, shows the letters taking a crooked path

explanation.surface: A cunning devil travels through the East incognito.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devious' scrambles DEVIL to VEILD, and 'touring' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Veiled means concealed or covered, as a disguise hides someone.

clue.text: Fibre, and estimate of how long it's been around?

parts.note: a rough figure is an estimate
age is how long something has existed

explanation.surface: A question about fibre and guessing something's age.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre is also called by this name, the indigestible bulk in food.

clue.text: Fine isn't collected by deputy on vacation

indicators.note: the contraction is gathered inside the outer letters
the word is emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial isn't

explanation.surface: A deputy away on holiday isn't paid a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty, but it is the adjective meaning delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dainty means delicate and fine, as in fine porcelain.

clue.text: Government finally delivers something to deal with the cold?

definitions.text: something to deal with the cold?

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: issues means hands out, delivers

explanation.surface: The government at last releases a remedy for the common cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is singular in form but means 'a thing for a cold', and paper hankies come in boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper handkerchiefs are what a sufferer reaches for with a runny nose.

clue.text: Scorer's firm marks a problem

parts.note: co is company, a firm
M stands for marks, the old German currency
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A footballer's club grades a tricky question.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes musical scores, so scorer in its musical sense.

clue.text: Ancient Scot on river shot

parts.note: the Picts lived in ancient Scotland
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An ancient Scotsman is shot beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a photograph, the same thing as a picture.

clue.text: Leo possibly completed what recruits do

parts.note: Leo is one example of a star sign
up means finished, as in time's up

explanation.surface: An astrologer's Leo has finished what new soldiers do.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruits enlist, the phrasal verb for joining up formally.

clue.text: Posh girls' establishment disposing of tutor?

parts.note: finishing means dealing with completely, disposing of
to school someone is to teach or tutor them

explanation.surface: Pupils at a smart girls' college get rid of their teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tutor' looks like a noun, a victim, but it is the verb, to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A private college where upper-class young women were taught etiquette and social graces.

clue.text: Mortgagee, they say, not the man for company

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the mortgagee is the lender, one who loans

explanation.surface: A lender isn't a sociable type.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner shuns company and prefers solitude.

clue.text: Disease that would be passed quickly by mouth when contracted

definitions.text: Disease that would be passed quickly by mouth when contracted

parts.words: Disease that would be passed quickly by mouth when contracted
parts.note: the illness's shortened name sounds like flew, which means passed quickly

explanation.surface: An illness that spreads fast by mouth once caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' means shortened: the short name FLU, spoken ('by mouth'), is FLEW, passed quickly. No wordplay builds the full answer's letters, so this is a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This viral illness spreads by airborne droplets, so it passes between mouths.

clue.text: Payment offered on a regular basis

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Money handed over at fixed intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a sum paid for a service.

clue.text: Were bachelor to join this marriage there'd be trouble afoot

indicators.note: the clue imagines the letter added; the solver removes it from the foot problem

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot
B is the degree abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A bachelor marrying would bring trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding B to the answer gives BUNION, so remove B from BUNION. 'afoot' is literally on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining, here the joining of two people as a married couple.

clue.text: Divine visitor almost succeeded

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a guest is a visitor
s for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A godlike visitor nearly made it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is a verb here, to work out by intuition.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to guess by intuition or insight.

clue.text: Before submission, one typically makes a claim

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a tender is a submitted bid

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a claim ahead of submitting a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender asserts a claim, classically to a throne.
